title: Emirates is bringing one of business travelers' favorite features to its premium economy cabins
summary:
Emirates unveiled a new premium-economy seat on Thursday, with a unique privacy screen.
However, premium economy passengers have typically had little to separate them from their neighbors.
Emirates' new seat also includes the U-Dream headrest that it revealed for the economy cabin at July's Farnborough Airshow.
They have 28 premium-economy seats in a 2-3-2 configuration.
With travelers willing to spend extra money for more luxury, premium economy bridges the gap to business class.

title: A political video network hired real actors to read its AI scripts. That was enough to beat YouTube’s detectors.
summary:
TL;DRYouTube has terminated a network of channels that reached 45 million views by paying gig-economy actors to read scripts that appear to have been generated by large language models.
That was the point, according to the media intelligence firm Riddance AI, which investigated the network in parallel with Semafor.
YouTube automatically labels AI-generated video whether creators disclose it or not, and a real person reading an AI script trips none of it.
Riddance found the 90,000-plus commenters substantially overlapped with audiences on other right-leaning YouTube channels, meaning actual people were watching.
The network out-engaged the YouTube channels of the Washington Post, the New Yorker and the Boston Globe, Semafor reported.

title: Why Innovation Now Depends on Resilience, Not Just Speed
summary:

Resilience depends on how fast you can adapt, not only on what you built.
For decades, innovation has been measured mostly by speed: who launched first, who built the next breakthrough, who disrupted an industry before anyone else could.
From building what’s next to preparing for what’s nextBusinesses today look very different from the ones many innovation strategies were built for.

title: Nvidia’s Hugging Face Acquisition Is a $12.9 Billion Bet on Open-Source AI
summary:
Nvidia has agreed to acquire Hugging Face, which makes online developer tools and maintains a massive library of open-source data sets, for nearly $13 billion.
Hugging Face was founded a decade ago by three French entrepreneurs in New York City, who wanted to launch an AI “companion” app.
“Open-source AI is at an inflection point,” wrote Hugging Face cofounder and CEO Clément Delangue in a post on X announcing the acquisition.
Hugging Face has more recently been front and center after its platform was hacked by AI agents from OpenAI.
And if all of them use Hugging Face all day, every day, we’ll obviously be in a good position.”Obviously, Nvidia seems to agree.

title: OpenAI’s Astra Is Here: What to Know About GPT-6
summary:
Like every model release, OpenAI says the new one (Astra) is better than the previous ones on a number of topics, including coding, alignment and safety.
Astra is also built to run more and better AI agents, or bots that can handle autonomous tasks.
To create Astra, OpenAI did “by far our largest scale training run,” Aidan Clark, vice president of research, told reporters on Thursday.
Astra was also OpenAI’s first model that involved previous AI models very heavily in the training process, with the older generations helping train the new one.
Jakub Pachocki, the company’s chief scientist, said international safety standards are necessary for the industry as AI models (and their capabilities) develop.

title: OpenAI is about to make its biggest push yet into the legal industry
summary:
Now, it's taking its case to law firms.
The ChatGPT maker is planning to launch new integrations with third-party legal software companies, according to people familiar with the matter.
The company has been in talks with multiple legal software providers about allowing OpenAI's chatbot to plug into their tools and data sources, the people said.
Law firms are under pressure from clients to move faster and show they're not billing associates for work that software can do.
That demand has produced a flood of startups addressing legal work.

title: GPT-6 Stole the Show, but Anthropic, Meta and Google Also Had New AI Models This Week
summary:
It wasn’t just OpenAI: Fellow AI heavy hitters Anthropic, Meta, and Google also announced updates to AI models.
Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1Anthropic announced updates for its Fable and Mythos models — both of which are some of the best available today.
Anthropic says that both Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 are the same model, but each has a different set of safeguards.
It also says that Fable 5.1, when set to low or medium effort, has performance similar to Fable 5 but at a much lower cost.
Gemini 3.8 and 3.8 Flash CyberGoogle released two new models in the form of Gemini 3.8 Flash and 3.8 Flash Cyber.

title: OpenAI's Sam Altman Sets Ambitious AI Goals Beyond Curing Cancer
summary:
Cure cancer with AI, and the doubters will understand the hype.
That may be Silicon Valley's standard pitch, but Sam Altman says it is not ambitious enough.
"I don't think a cure for cancer is enough," Altman said.
Altman said AI should also "enable a boom in creativity and entrepreneurship," but that this has "been lost in the messaging."
Altman's cancer comments stand in contrast to Dario Amodei, the CEO of AI rival Anthropic, who said last month that the way to win over the public is for AI to "actually" cure cancer.

title: CrowdStrike put OpenAI in the product and Anthropic at the checkout
summary:
CrowdStrike said on Wednesday that it will run OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Cyber inside a purpose-built cyber harness.
Its Frontier AI Readiness and Resilience service applies GPT-5.6 Cyber “within CrowdStrike’s purpose-built cyber harness”.
Policing the agents it also sellsThe other half is Falcon Guardian, CrowdStrike’s AI detection and response product, applied to Codex agents.
Anthropic turns up on the other side of the counterFive hours later CrowdStrike announced a second deal, this time with Anthropic.
It also introduced an Agentic Identity Provider, which issues AI agents their own identities and treats that as the control plane for the enterprise.

title: Instagram’s AI detection is a mess (again)
summary:
They say Meta has been automatically applying an “AI Content” label to images that they didn’t create or edit using generative AI tools.
In 2024, the detection system reportedly swept up pictures whose Adobe metadata indicated they had been retouched with generative AI tools, even if the changes were extremely minor and substantively resulted in the same photograph.
These are just some of the images I posted to Instagram to test its AI detection, but only the two on the top right (created in Meta AI) were tagged.
That said, only a handful should add generative AI metadata to photographs: Spatial Reframing, Extend, and updated Clean Up added in iOS 27.
The results have left me questioning if there is any sense in how Meta is applying “AI Content” tags.

title: Why AI food looks like that
summary:
There are many reasons why this AI food is so wrong, from the technical nuances of how AI systems generate images and the materials used to train them to the psychological baggage humans perceive the images through.
That helps explain why so many AI food images are so relentlessly noodly, unsettlingly patterned, and riddled with the kind of clustered holes that can trigger trypophobia.
AI models have no understanding of why food should not look like other non-food images in that way.
A lot of popular AI material involves food, Cook said, recalling a trend for AI-generated videos of people jumping in or on piles of food.
AI generated food looks wrong because, on a primal level, it feels wrong.

title: Dyson’s new straightener has liquid cooling pipes to reduce hair damage
summary:
The $329 Corrale CoolShine straightener upgrades the original Corrale that launched in 2020 with active cooling technology designed to “reduce residual heatexposure” so hair feels smoother, softer, and cooler to the touch after styling.
Alongside it is the new $249 Dyson Airsmooth dryer brush designed for both drying and styling hair using a new anti-snag bristle technology developed by the company.
Those precisely controlled heating elements are now joined by water-filled pipes that draw excess heat away from hair as it’s being pulled through the straightener.
So in a single pass, hair is being heated, straightened, and then cooled back down to help reduce potential damage from being heated too long.
The Airsmooth dryer brush features a unique teardrop-shaped design and looped bristles engineered to reduce snags while brushing.

title: T-Mobile’s Gopalan turns to home internet and AI after a 25% slide
summary:
T-Mobile US chief executive Srini Gopalan is selling home internet and AI as the growth story.
Elliott Investment Management has built a stake in parent Deutsche Telekom and wants the plan dropped in favour of buybacks.
A new holding company would make an all-share bid for both and list on both sides of the Atlantic.
A full merger would cut the combined state holding to roughly 17%, below the 25% that carries a blocking minority under German company law.
T-Mobile’s own executives told Deutsche Telekom in August that they no longer support it.

title: Zuckerberg Told Trump a National AI Regulator Is a Flawed Idea
summary:
White House officials envision the group reviewing advanced models and testing them for potential risks before they are deployed more broadly.
The idea for an AI regulator was popularized by Hassabis, who suggested in a July essay that the US establish a new "standards body" modeled after FINRA to handle AI risks such as emerging cybersecurity threats.
Hassabis briefed White House officials about the concept this summer, according to an administration official familiar with the matter.
The call with Zuckerberg did not quash the idea of a new industry regulator and it remains under consideration in the White House.
David Sacks, former Trump AI advisor, and Mark Zuckerberg, during a White House dinner with tech leaders on Sept. 4, 2025.

title: OpenAI does a victory lap for its new AI model: 'Welcome to the AGI era'
summary:
OpenAI says that its new model has reached the AI industry's most sought-after milestone.
"Welcome to the AGI era," Greg Brockman, the company's president, said at the end of a press call announcing the arrival of OpenAI's Astra model on Thursday.
AGI stands for artificial general intelligence, a fuzzy concept that nonetheless has become a core goal for AI development.
"Anything you can do on a computer, Astra can do for you.
Fast," OpenAI wrote on X.

title: Google says its AI weather model is getting better
summary:
Google is rolling out an updated AI weather model that’s supposed to be more accurate, especially when it comes to predicting rain and snowfall.
AI weather models created by Google and other developers, in contrast, can make faster predictions by recognizing patterns in historical weather data.
Image: GoogleGoogle also designed its latest AI weather model to produce forecasts for renewable energy generation.
Google has also worked with the US National Hurricane Center and other agencies in Asia to improve weather forecasting using its AI models.
While AI models are becoming more accurate, they’re still expected to work in tandem with traditional physics-based models.

title: Sam Altman says AI developers have fumbled at communicating the technology’s benefits
summary:
Sam Altman says the AI industry has done a terrible job of communicating the benefits of the technology and is now exposed to a backlash, after local opposition blocked or delayed 75 data centre projects worth about $130B in a single quarter.
Sam Altman says the AI industry has done a terrible job of explaining what the technology is for.
At least 75 data centre projects worth about $130B were blocked or delayed by local opposition in the first three months of this year.
Danish data centre capacity stood at 398MW at the start of the year, with a further 208MW under construction.
A data centre energy efficiency package and the Cloud and AI Development Act would tie public support to energy, water and circularity performance.
